newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit weaker vs dollar, seen testing 2.5200.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit weaker vs dollar, seen testing 2.5200.

text.p: * Ringgit weaker on dollar demand out of Sydney
* Sentiment still affected by huge trade deficit in April
* Sales of ringgit/Sing cross also pressured ringgit
The ringgit was weaker against the dollar in early Asian trading on further dollar buying by offshore players, dealers said.
"Sydney was buying the dollar this morning and we may see demand from other offshore centres through the day," said a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur. "The ringgit looks weak at the moment."
He said dollar/ringgit was likely to test the 2.5200 level and "possibly a minor break to 2.5220."
Selling of ringgit/Singapore dollar cross also pressured the Malaysian unit, dealers said.

They said ringgit sentiment remained affected by an unexpectedly huge Malaysian trade deficit in April announced on Friday. Malaysia announced a trade deficit of 2.1 billion ringgit in April after a 1.75 billion ringgit surplus in March.
But downside for the ringgit was expected to be limited as dollar sentiment was also weak, dealers said.
They said there could be strong ringgit support at 2.5200, the level Bank Negara was last heard checking.
At 0200 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5170/80 a dollar against 2.5155/65 at close in Kuala Lumpur on Monday.
